title: Rupee seen weakening to 97 per dollar by FY27 end amid global risks: BMI
description:
The Indian rupee is expected to weaken further against the US dollar over the next two fiscal years, pressured by elevated energy prices, global risk aversion and less favourable interest-rate differentials, while government measures to attract foreign capital should help contain the pace of depreciation, BMI, a Fitch Solutions Company, said.
BMI expects the rupee to weaken to Rs 97 per US dollar by the end of FY2026-27, which runs from April 2026 to March 2027, and to Rs 99 per dollar by the end of FY2027-28, from Rs 95.4 currently.
The currency has already weakened by about 4 per cent since the start of the US-Iran conflict, with higher energy prices and a broader risk-off environment weighing on the rupee, the research firm said in a note.
